sections.markdown:
## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: lane added versus merge, HOV eligibility, exit lane markers, diamond versus cloverleaf turns, weaving lanes, safe interstate habits, message signs, congestion causes, Move Over sides, breakdown help and emergency kit
Confusable pairs and continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and any hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec10-R01 | anchor: A01
Interstates and divided highways have largely eliminated the risk of head-on collisions, and they usually have few steep hills or sharp curves. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec10-R02 | anchor: A01
Drivers already on the interstate should, for their own safety, make room for vehicles trying to enter, even though the entering driver must yield. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec10-R03 | anchor: A01
Driving at an even speed reduces the need to change lanes, and lane-hopping raises crash risk, feeds road rage and rarely saves real time. [A01]
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0082]

FACT_ID: sec10-R04 | anchor: A02
Avoid traveling in packs of cars and keep a space cushion around you for emergency moves. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec10-R05 | anchor: A02
Drivers in every lane except the right-hand slow lane should be ready to move over so faster traffic can pass. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec10-R06 | anchor: A02
Trucks and buses joining the interstate may need extra time and space to fit into traffic, so give it to them. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec10-R07 | anchor: A02
HOV lanes sit at the far inside of the interstate, so to use one you merge onto the highway normally and then move across to the far inside lane. [A02]
Why it matters: group HOV; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec10-R08 | anchor: A02
Buses need two or more occupants to use the HOV lane at peak hours, while a motorcycle qualifies with just its rider. [A02]
Why it matters: group HOV; confusable bus occupancy versus motorcycle occupancy.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec10-R09 | anchor: A02
If you plan to exit before the HOV lane ends, you must carefully move back across to the exit lane. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec10-R10 | anchor: A03
The deceleration lane at an exit is usually outlined by a row of white reflectors. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-R11 | anchor: A03
At a cloverleaf, turning right means taking the right-hand ramp before the overpass, and the loop for a left turn leaves you heading as if you had turned left. [A03]
Why it matters: group interchanges; confusable cloverleaf right versus left ramps.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-R12 | anchor: A03
A cloverleaf's advantage is that no turn crosses the path of other traffic. [A03]
Why it matters: group interchanges; confusable cloverleaf versus diamond.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-R13 | anchor: A03
At a weaving interchange, follow routine on-ramp entry procedures while watching for interstate vehicles moving right toward the exit ramp, with both drivers yielding and sharing in an equal give-and-take manner [A03].
Why it matters: group interchanges; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec10-R14 | anchor: A04
Left turns and U-turns on the interstate are allowed only through an opening provided and marked for them, and only emergency and maintenance crews may cross the median. [A04]
Why it matters: group prohibited moves; confusable marked opening versus emergency crossover.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec10-R15 | anchor: A04
Stopping or parking on the interstate is allowed only in areas provided for it, and parking on the shoulder only in an emergency. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec10-R16 | anchor: A04
Good interstate habits include signaling well ahead, checking mirrors often, keeping a safe following distance and checking your speed and fuel gauges often. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec10-R17 | anchor: A04
Watch for pedestrians from broken-down vehicles, animals on the road and drivers going the wrong way. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec10-R18 | anchor: A04
Following too closely causes many multiple-car crashes, and higher interstate speeds call for longer gaps. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec10-R19 | anchor: A04
Dynamic Message Signs on urban Tennessee interstates, part of TDOT's SmartWay system, show real-time crash, weather and construction news, travel times and Amber Alerts, and are blank when not in use. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec10-R20 | anchor: A05
Vehicles that run out of gas or break down from poor maintenance can cause bottlenecks, so watch your fuel and maintain your car. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-R21 | anchor: A05
When the stopped vehicle is on the right shoulder, move into the left lane; when it is on the left shoulder, move into the right lane, leaving the nearest lane empty. [A05]
Why it matters: group move over; confusable right shoulder versus left shoulder.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-R22 | anchor: A05
The Move Over Law covers police and Highway Patrol cars, ambulances and fire vehicles, utility and sanitation trucks, tow trucks, TDOT HELP and maintenance vehicles, and road contractors. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-R23 | anchor: A05
If your car breaks down and you need help, raise the hood and tie a white cloth to the hood or antenna, and if possible wait in or near the car on the side away from traffic. [A05]
Why it matters: group breakdowns; confusable waiting in versus beside the car.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-R24 | anchor: A05
Walking along the interstate is dangerous, so keep children away from traffic, and a passing officer not on another call will stop to help a driver who stays with the vehicle. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-R25 | anchor: A05
In Memphis, Nashville, Chattanooga and Knoxville, yellow TDOT HELP trucks may also assist stranded drivers. [A05]
Why it matters: group breakdowns; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec10-R26 | anchor: A06
HELP operators may remove any vehicle that obstructs or endangers traffic, and you must follow their directions as you would a police officer's. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-R27 | anchor: A06
While waiting at a crash scene you must stay, but you should not block traffic unnecessarily; TDOT signs remind drivers to move damaged vehicles to the shoulder when no one is seriously hurt. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-R28 | anchor: A06
A suggested roadside emergency kit includes an excellent spare tire, jack and tire iron, tire pressure gauge, flashlight with spare batteries, first aid kit, fire extinguisher, jumper cables, three fuses or reflectors, insurance and registration papers, and a cell phone [A06].
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec10-R29 | anchor: A06
For winter trips also carry a blanket, a small portable heater, an ice scraper and snow tires or chains, and in summer carry bottled water. [A06]
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0087]
